title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated video and images to create hundreds of fake social media profiles impersonating a real immigration attorney. The fake profiles promoted immigration services the attorney did not offer, including US residency assistance for a specific fee to undocumented immigrants. This is impersonation enabled by generative AI, deployed at scale across social media platforms to defraud vulnerable people seeking legal help.

The scheme operated on social media without meaningful platform verification of the attorney's identity. Victims were directed to messaging apps where they received fraudulent contracts and requests for payment through consumer money transfer services. Catching this would have required either identity verification at account creation on social media platforms, or human review of accounts making legal service claims before they accumulated thousands of followers.

Whether the social media platforms bore responsibility for the fraud or the extent of any platform liability remains not established.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, reports that scammers are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal promoting immigration services he never offers. In one video, the fake Leal advertises US residency assistance for $2,200 to undocumented immigrants without deportation orders. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity first appeared in October. The situation has significantly worsened over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. Scammers typically direct victims through social media videos to WhatsApp, where they send fraudulent contracts and request payment via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams. He advises immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of immediate payment requests.
